Class SmoothMath

java.lang.Object
org.ether.society.core.math.SmoothMath
public final class SmoothMath extends Object
Stateless \(O(1)\) infinitely differentiable (\(C^\infty\)) analytical primitives for biophysical and cliodynamic differential equations.

Replaces discontinuous boolean thresholds, ternary step cliffs, and \(C^0\) piecewise-linear corners (Math.max(0, x - x0), Math.min(a, b), Math.clamp) with numerically stable, overflow-safe closed-form expressions grounded in statistical mechanics:

  • Fermi-Dirac Sigmoid: \(\sigma(x; x_0, s) = \frac{1}{1 + \exp(-(x - x_0)/s)}\)
  • Softplus: \(\operatorname{softplus}(x; x_0, s) = s \ln\left(1 + \exp\left(\frac{x - x_0}{s}\right)\right)\)
  • LogSumExp Softmax / Softmin: smooth Liebig law of the minimum without derivative kinks
  • Smooth Clamp: \(\operatorname{sclamp}(x, a, b; s) = a + \operatorname{softplus}(x; a, s) - \operatorname{softplus}(x; b, s)\)
  • Garrett Harmonic Coupling: \(C^\infty\) complementary bound \(h(a, b) = \frac{a \cdot b}{a + b + \varepsilon}\)

  • Method Details

    • sigmoid

      public static double sigmoid(double x, double x0, double scale)
      Evaluates the \(C^\infty\) Fermi-Dirac logistic sigmoid \(\sigma(x; x_0, s) \in (0, 1)\).

      $$\sigma(x; x_0, s) = \frac{1}{1 + \exp\!\left(-\frac{x - x_0}{s}\right)}$$

      Parameters:
      x - input physical observable
      x0 - inflection midpoint (\(\sigma(x_0; x_0, s) = 0.5\))
      scale - strictly positive transition width \(s > 0\) in physical units of x
      Returns:
      smooth activation weight in \((0, 1)\)

    • softplus

      public static double softplus(double x, double x0, double sharpness)
      Evaluates the \(C^\infty\) scaled softplus function, providing a globally differentiable replacement for the \(C^0\) ramp \(\max(0, x - x_0)\).

      $$\operatorname{softplus}(x; x_0, k) = \frac{\ln\!\left(1 + \exp(k(x - x_0))\right)}{k}$$

      Its first derivative is strictly \(\frac{d}{dx}\operatorname{softplus}(x; x_0, k) = \sigma(x; x_0, 1/k) \in (0, 1)\).

      Parameters:
      x - input physical observable
      x0 - onset reference point
      sharpness - transition sharpness \(k > 0\)
      Returns:
      strictly positive \(C^\infty\) ramp value

    • softmax

      public static double softmax(double a, double b, double sharpness)
      Evaluates the \(C^\infty\) LogSumExp smooth maximum of two physical observables.

      $$\operatorname{softmax}(a, b; k) = m + \frac{\ln\!\left(1 + \exp(-k |a - b|)\right)}{k}, \quad m = \max(a, b)$$

      Parameters:
      a - first observable
      b - second observable
      sharpness - smoothing sharpness \(k > 0\)
      Returns:
      smooth upper envelope \(\ge \max(a, b)\)

    • softmin

      public static double softmin(double a, double b, double sharpness)
      Evaluates the \(C^\infty\) LogSumExp smooth minimum (differentiable Liebig Law of the Minimum).

      $$\operatorname{softmin}(a, b; k) = -\operatorname{softmax}(-a, -b; k)$$

      Parameters:
      a - first limiting factor
      b - second limiting factor
      sharpness - smoothing sharpness \(k > 0\)
      Returns:
      smooth lower envelope \(\le \min(a, b)\)

    • smoothClamp

      public static double smoothClamp(double x, double min, double max, double sharpness)
      Evaluates a \(C^\infty\) smooth interval saturation replacing piecewise Math.clamp(x, min, max).

      $$\operatorname{sclamp}(x, a, b; k) = \operatorname{softmin}(b, \operatorname{softmax}(a, x; k); k)$$

      Parameters:
      x - input observable
      min - asymptotic lower bound \(a\)
      max - asymptotic upper bound \(b > a\)
      sharpness - transition sharpness \(k > 0\)
      Returns:
      smoothly bounded value strictly inside \((a, b)\)

    • harmonicCoupling

      public static double harmonicCoupling(double a, double b)
      Evaluates Garrett's (2011) \(C^\infty\) harmonic complementarity bound between two positive capacities (e.g., gross structural capital per capita \(k\) and energized maintenance capacity \(k_{\text{energized}}\)).

      $$h(a, b) = \frac{a \cdot b}{a + b + \varepsilon}$$

      Satisfies \(0 \le h(a, b) \le \min(a, b)\): if either input approaches \(0\), the harmonic coupling smoothly vanishes without derivative discontinuities.

      Parameters:
      a - first non-negative physical capacity
      b - second non-negative physical capacity
      Returns:
      harmonically coupled active capacity
